adjudication_reasoning: The paper uses deep learning semantic segmentation of crop/weed in precision agriculture but the focus is adaptive UAV path planning and an altitude-vs-accuracy model; it reports no concrete quantitative segmentation metric (no mIoU/Dice/F1/PA) on the field data. Per the adjudication rule, a segmentation-for-other-purpose paper that lacks a concrete segmentation accuracy number is excluded under EXC-06.

ViTs are applied to whole-image 'plant classification' of weeds/crops in UAV images of beet, parsley and spinach; the objective and reported results (ViT vs EfficientNet/ResNet) are image classification, not pixel-level segmentation masks. This is whole-image classification with no pixel-wise segmentation, so it violates EXC-02.

The method detects crop rows and interline weeds then trains CNNs to 'detect the crop and weeds in the images', with results given as classification accuracy gaps (1.5% spinach, 6% bean). No pixel-level segmentation masks or segmentation metric are reported; it is crop/weed detection/classification without segmentation masks.

The task is Rumex image classification (whole-image) via ResNets and DINOv2 ViTs reporting classification F1=0.8, with a source ground-vehicle dataset and UAV target dataset. It is whole-image classification with no segmentation masks, so it is excluded under EXC-02.

The framework detects insect pests with a lightweight CNN (prototypical meta-learning) for pesticide recommendation, which is pest detection rather than crop/weed pixel segmentation. It is a bounding-box/object-detection task in the pest-management domain, not crop/weed segmentation, so it violates EXC-03 and EXC-02.

A semi-supervised GAN provides pixel-wise classification of crop/weed on the weedNet MAV dataset (semantic segmentation, INC-01), but the abstract reports only 'high classification accuracy' with no concrete quantitative metric (no mIoU/Dice/F1/PA). Under EXC-06 no retrievable quantitative segmentation result is given.

This is on-policy RL (PPO) for multi-UAV area exploration/coverage using actor-critic CNN-LSTM networks; it is neither semantic segmentation nor agricultural crop/weed analysis. It falls outside the agronomic scope under EXC-03.

SugarViT is a Vision Transformer for disease-severity scoring (Cercospora Leaf Spot) of sugar beet via regression/classification, not crop/weed pixel segmentation. It is a disease-scoring classification task, violating EXC-02 and the disease-classification exclusion in EXC-03.

TreeScope is a LiDAR dataset for semantic segmentation and diameter estimation of tree stems in forests and orchards (arboriculture/forestry). Tree mapping in forestry/orchards is outside agricultural crop/weed management, so it is excluded under EXC-03.

Though it reports segmentation metrics (U-Net/YOLOv11m-seg/Mask R-CNN; F1=0.86, mIoU=0.72) and throughput, the target is olive tree crown/shadow segmentation for biovolume estimation in orchards. Permanent orchard fruit-tree analysis is clearly outside crop/weed arable agronomy, so it is excluded under EXC-03.

SkySeg is a collaborative onboard semantic-segmentation framework for generic UAV remote-sensing missions with no agricultural crop/weed context; reported gains (3.6x latency, 5.91% accuracy) are on general scenes. There is no crop/weed agronomy, so it is excluded under EXC-03.

S3M performs semantic-segmentation SLAM mapping for indoor UAV search-and-rescue navigation (RGB-D, OctoMap, Gazebo). This is indoor navigation/robotics, not agricultural crop/weed segmentation, so it is excluded under EXC-03.

UVid-Net is a CNN for UAV video semantic segmentation evaluated on the ManipalUAVid urban street-scene dataset (mIoU 0.79); the classes are generic urban scenes, not crop/weed. It is outside agricultural crop/weed agronomy, so it is excluded under EXC-03.

This neuromorphic SNN semantic-segmentation study is evaluated on the DSEC driving-scene dataset for UAV/self-driving real-time systems; it balances latency/accuracy/energy on urban driving scenes, not crop/weed agronomy. It is excluded under EXC-03.

Real-time multi-modal LiDAR/RGB semantic fusion on UAVs is evaluated for urban disaster examination; the abstract has no crop/weed agricultural content. It is an urban scene-analysis system, excluded under EXC-03.

PBSeg prototype-based semantic segmentation achieves 71.86% mIoU on UAVid and 80.92% on UDD6, both urban aerial datasets; classes are urban scenes, not crop/weed. It falls outside agricultural crop/weed agronomy under EXC-03.

The study benchmarks real-time semantic segmentation of flood-affected buildings/roads on the Flood-Net hurricane UAV dataset, a disaster-response domain. There is no crop/weed agronomy, so it is excluded under EXC-03.

Segmentation-architecture analysis (FPN-EfficientNetB3, IoU 0.65, F1 0.71, memory/latency) is run on the DroneDeploy general aerial segmentation benchmark; no crop/weed agricultural context is established. It is excluded under EXC-03 as a generic UAV scene-segmentation study.
Multi-modal LiDAR/RGB semantic fusion with label propagation is deployed for urban and disaster scenes (9 Hz); there is no agricultural crop/weed context. It is excluded under EXC-03.

Co-SemDepth jointly performs depth and semantic segmentation on MidAir/Aeroscapes for autonomous UAV navigation (20.2 FPS); scenes are generic aerial environments, not crop/weed. It is excluded under EXC-03.

SNN semantic segmentation is trained on PASCAL VOC2012 and DDD17 driving/event datasets; there is no crop/weed agricultural content. It is a general/urban semantic segmentation study, excluded under EXC-03.

Memory-constrained semantic segmentation of ultra-high-resolution UAV imagery is evaluated on generic public benchmarks without any crop/weed agricultural context. It reports no crop/weed domain, so it is excluded under EXC-03.

Adaptive Model Streaming for real-time edge video semantic segmentation targets generic video datasets (multiple video datasets, 30 FPS on a phone). No agricultural crop/weed content, so it is excluded under EXC-03.

FBSNet real-time semantic segmentation is benchmarked on Cityscapes and CamVid driving scenes (mIoU 70.9%/68.9%, 90/120 FPS). This is an autonomous-driving/urban scene task, not crop/weed, so it is excluded under EXC-03.
Hyperbolic uncertainty-aware segmentation (HyperUL) is evaluated on Cityscapes and UAVid urban scenes; classes are general city/urban, not crop/weed. It is excluded under EXC-03.

Vision-transformer compression is demonstrated for UAV edge deployment aimed at navigation, surveillance and search-and-rescue, with no crop/weed agricultural segmentation. It is a general model-compression study excluded under EXC-03.
MSCFNet real-time lightweight segmentation is evaluated on the Cityscapes driving dataset (71.9% mIoU, >50 FPS). It is an autonomous-driving urban task, not crop/weed, so it is excluded under EXC-03.

ArmFormer is a lightweight transformer for multi-class weapon (handgun, rifle, knife, revolver) semantic segmentation targeting security cameras and surveillance drones (80.64% mIoU, 82.26 FPS). This is a security/surveillance domain, not crop/weed, so it is excluded under EXC-03.

Energy-efficient edge crack segmentation (KD+PTQ+FPGA, 398 FPS, custom U-Net on CrackVision12K, mean IoU 69.42%) supports infrastructure/bridge inspection with UAVs. This is civil-infrastructure monitoring, not crop/weed, so it is excluded under EXC-03.

TSJNet is a multimodal infrared-visible image-fusion network evaluated on MSRS, M3FD, RoadScene, TNO for generic segmentation/detection; no crop/weed agricultural content is present. It is excluded under EXC-03.

H2O-Net segments floods primarily from satellite imagery (10%/12% gains), a flood/disaster domain that is not agricultural crop/weed. The primary modality is satellite rather than UAV, violating EXC-01, and the domain is outside crop/weed agronomy under EXC-03.

A SegFormer-based model segments hotspots and snail trails in solar PV thermal imagery captured by a drone (DJI Matrice 100) over solar farms. This is energy-infrastructure inspection, not crop/weed, so it is excluded under EXC-03.

This is a 'reading report' synthesizing AI/ML for wireless dynamic spectrum sensing and Open RAN — secondary literature on wireless networks, not an agricultural crop/weed segmentation benchmark. It is excluded under EXC-05 (secondary) and EXC-03 (out of domain).

SafeLand uses semantic segmentation (70.22% mIoU over 20 classes) for autonomous UAV safe landing in urban/rural environments near people and infrastructure. This is aerial-robotics landing, not crop/weed agronomy, so it is excluded under EXC-03.

A multi-task multi-stage network does satellite/aerial scene interpretation and geolocalization, evaluated on Inria and Massachusetts Buildings urban building datasets for GPS-level localization. It is an urban remote-sensing task, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.

This work performs 3D instance segmentation of MVS buildings in urban scenes (roofs/buildings), a geospatial/urban remote-sensing task. There is no crop/weed agricultural content, so it is excluded under EXC-03.

Network slimming with nonconvex regularization is demonstrated on VGG-19, DenseNet-40, and ResNet-164 for generic image classification datasets. It is a model-compression method with no crop/weed segmentation content, excluded under EXC-03.

CARLA2Real is a sim2real tool for the CARLA simulator aligning output to Cityscapes/KITTI/Mapillary Vistas for autonomous driving; it is an autonomous-driving sim-to-real study, not crop/weed. It is excluded under EXC-03.

CAWM-Mamba performs infrared-visible image fusion and compound-weather restoration for autonomous driving and UAV monitoring (AWMM-100K benchmark); downstream tasks are generic segmentation/detection, not crop/weed. It is excluded under EXC-03.

A cloud-edge AI architecture detects tomato plant diseases (early/late blight, leaf mold) via a TensorFlow classification model on PlantVillage/Kaggle (92-95% detection). This is disease-classification, not crop/weed pixel segmentation, violating EXC-03 and EXC-02.

GUARD uses YOLO-based deer object detection for wildlife deterrence on a farmland UAV; it is bounding-box wildlife detection, not crop/weed segmentation. Domain and task are outside scope under EXC-03 and EXC-02.

This is an exploratory/popular article describing drone types and advantages in agriculture with no primary empirical benchmark or quantitative segmentation results. It is secondary/non-empirical literature, excluded under EXC-05.

A quantum-resilient blockchain framework secures data/transactions in UAV smart-agriculture networks using post-quantum cryptography and consensus protocols. This is a network-security paper with no computer-vision crop/weed segmentation, excluded under EXC-03.

AeroDaaS is a Drones-as-a-Service programming framework for aerial analytics microservices, evaluated for platform overhead (<20 ms/frame on Orin Nano) rather than any crop/weed segmentation. It is a systems/framework paper, excluded under EXC-03.

An apple-orchard pipeline does leaf-disease classification (ResNet50), freshness classification (VGG16) and YOLOv8 apple object detection — fruit-domain classification/detection, not crop/weed pixel segmentation. It violates EXC-03 (fruit) and EXC-02 (detection/classification).

DroneFL is a federated-learning framework for multi-UAV target tracking via a frozen YOLO backbone and trajectory transformer; it is target tracking/trajectory prediction, not crop/weed segmentation. It is excluded under EXC-03.

YOLOv11-Litchi is a bounding-box object-detection model for litchi fruit in orchard UAV imagery (mAP 90.1%, 57.2 FPS). It is fruit-domain object detection with no segmentation masks, violating EXC-03 (fruit) and EXC-02.

Per-tree canopy volume estimation uses mobile LiDAR segmentation (DBSCAN + spectral clustering) in pistachio and almond orchards, validated against drone-derived volume. This is orchard/arboriculture per-tree phenotyping, not crop/weed management, excluded under EXC-03.

A wireless whispering-gallery-mode optical sensor is demonstrated for thermal sensing and aerial temperature mapping mounted on a drone; there is no deep-learning crop/weed segmentation. It is an IoT/photonic-sensor hardware study, excluded under EXC-03.

The system segments cranberry fruit for sun-exposure/overheating-risk assessment (62.54% mIoU), a berry-fruit phenotyping task rather than crop/weed agronomy management. As a fruit-focused phenotyping application it is treated as outside crop/weed scope under EXC-03.

Encoder-decoder CNNs perform pixel-wise crop/weed classification/segmentation on ground and aerial images, including a third CNN specifically for small-UAV (UAV-borne) setups, with 'quantitative experimental results' on multiple public datasets. This is in-scope DL UAV-capable crop/weed pixel segmentation reporting metrics.

SemiWeedNet is a DNN-based semi-supervised semantic segmentation method for weed and crop identification on a publicly available dataset, reporting results that outperform state-of-the-art methods. It is an empirical DL crop/weed segmentation benchmark with quantitative results; while the abstract does not state the UAV platform, it is not a clearly non-UAV modality, so it is not excluded.

The study uses UAV multispectral thermal imaging to extract tea-canopy temperature for crop water-shortage diagnosis and irrigation decisions. This is crop water-stress detection, not crop/weed pixel segmentation, and reports no quantitative segmentation metric, so it is excluded under EXC-03 and EXC-06.

Weed-patch detection in wheat uses vegetation indices, Object-Based Image Analysis and connected-component classification — classical image processing, not deep learning. This violates the deep-learning requirement under EXC-04.

The SWD framework classifies sugarcane weeds using pretrained ResNet18/VGG16/MobileNet CNNs (95.2% classification accuracy) and estimates yield via LAI; although it masks soil background, the core task is weed-crop classification, not pixel-level segmentation masks. It is excluded under EXC-02.

D2S2-UI is a diffusion-driven synthetic dataset for generalized aerial semantic segmentation across diverse terrains and regions (multi-altitude, land-cover classes), with no specific crop/weed focus. It is a general aerial-scene dataset, excluded under EXC-03 as not crop/weed agronomy.

DeepLab v3+ performs crop/weed semantic segmentation to locate weed patches in sugarcane drones, but the reported quantitative outcomes (66.3% route-time/energy reduction) are path-planning metrics, with no pixel-wise segmentation accuracy (mIoU/Dice/F1/PA) given. Lacking a concrete segmentation metric, it is excluded under EXC-06.

The InceptionResNetV2-UNet model segments satellite imagery, motivated by satellite-picture segmentation challenges, with no UAV aerial crop/weed content. The primary modality is satellite, violating EXC-01.

HDR-Net (YOLOv8n + U-Net++) performs instance segmentation of water hyacinth, an invasive aquatic weed in a river catchment on UAV RGB/multispectral imagery (Dice 0.946). This is aquatic/invasive ecosystem weed mapping for biosecurity, not agricultural crop/weed agronomy, so it is excluded under EXC-03 (aquatic).

No abstract is available despite a title indicating UAV multispectral weed segmentation and classification; no retrievable quantitative results exist to evaluate against the criteria. It is excluded under EXC-06.

A drone-based weed-detection/application-map framework localizes Canada Thistle in sugarbeets and Rumex in grasslands using bounding-box-style detection for spraying (88% weeds sprayed, 85% herbicide saved), not pixel-level segmentation masks. It is excluded under EXC-02.

Transformer and CNN models (SegFormer, DPT, UPerNet, U-Net, DeepLabv3+, PSPNet) perform pixel-level semantic segmentation of sunflower inflorescences on a UAV RGB orthomosaic, with DPT reaching F-score 0.946 and IoU 0.897 plus computational-cost analysis. This is DL crop pixel-segmentation on UAV imagery reporting quantitative metrics, in scope for RQ1; sunflower is a field crop, not fruit/forestry/livestock.

No abstract is available and the title indicates a broad review of drone technology for precision agriculture and livestock farming. As secondary/review literature without a primary UAV crop/weed segmentation benchmark, it is excluded under EXC-05 (and EXC-06 for no abstract/metrics).

UAS imagery is used to derive crop-weed leaf-area ratios to predict maize yield loss via a linear regression model (r2 0.97). The task is yield-regression based on imagery-derived cover, not deep-learning crop/weed pixel segmentation, so it violates EXC-02 (task) and EXC-04 (no DL segmentation).
No abstract is available despite a title indicating UAV deep-learning cotton weed detection; no retrievable quantitative results exist to screen. It is excluded under EXC-06.

The abstract proposes a taxonomy/synthesis organizing existing UAV-based crop-disease and weed-detection research loosely around disease diagnosis, i.e., secondary literature with no primary empirical segmentation benchmark. It is excluded under EXC-05 (secondary/taxonomy) and EXC-03 (disease-classification domain).

A context-aware slimmable-network compression framework performs on-UAV weed detection via bounding boxes, with gains measured in computation reduction (up to 35% fewer FLOPs) and small accuracy improvement. It is object detection without pixel-level segmentation masks, excluded under EXC-02.

Agrochemi-Net detects crops via a CNN bounding-box object detector and segments weeds using a Genetic-Algorithm-optimized color index (non-deep-learned). The crop task is bounding-box detection and the weed method is not deep learning, violating EXC-02 and EXC-04.

An improved Mask R-CNN performs weed instance segmentation on resource-limited weeding robots (ground vehicles), with the drone acting as a wireless edge server. The primary imaging modality is ground-robot weeding rather than UAV-borne aerial crop/weed imagery, so it is excluded under EXC-01.

A vision-based crop-row (line) detection system supports UAV weed detection in arboriculture/tree-nursery beds; the task is row/line detection rather than pixel-level crop-weed segmentation, and arboriculture is outside arable crop/weed agronomy. It is excluded under EXC-02 and EXC-03.

UAV photogrammetry detects, segments, classifies and measures tree stumps and root/butt-rot in post-harvest forestry sites (68-80% detection accuracy). This is a forestry application, outside agricultural crop/weed management, excluded under EXC-03.

A three-stage DL framework (ResNet50 + DeepLabV3+) classifies and segments structural damage (crack/corrosion/spalling) for UAV bridge/offshore infrastructure inspection (mIoU 0.789). This is a civil-infrastructure domain, entirely outside crop/weed agronomy, excluded under EXC-03.

Line detection combined with semantic segmentation extracts power lines from UAV images for power-line inspection (multi-scale LSD, OMRF, Kalman filter). This is infrastructure inspection, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.
Fast-SCNN and BiSeNetV2 are benchmarked for real-time flood segmentation in UAV imagery (F1 0.738). This is a flood-monitoring/disaster domain, not agricultural crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.

Olive-tree crown detection uses local-extrema and object-based multiresolution segmentation (Gaussian filter + OBIA) on UAV orthomosaic/CHM, which is non-deep-learning and orchard/arboriculture rather than crop/weed. It is excluded under EXC-04 (no DL) and EXC-03 (orchard domain).

Coverage-aware training of YOLO11-seg/DeepLabV3+ segments buildings and roads for drone localization in AAM/UAM urban mobility (>60 FPS). This is an urban building/road domain for navigation, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.

This is a peer-review record ('Review: ... R3/PR15') of a tree-crown semantic segmentation paper; the underlying work performs forest tree-species crown segmentation (mIoU 55.97%). As a review/secondary record of a forestry-tree paper, it is excluded under EXC-05 and EXC-03.

This is a peer-review record ('Review: ... R1/PR6') of a tree-crown semantic segmentation paper (forest tree-species, mIoU 55.97%). It is secondary review literature in the forestry domain, excluded under EXC-05 and EXC-03.

An improved DeepLabV3+ (MobileNetV2 + CBAM) segments cultivated land parcels (field boundaries) from mountainous UAV imagery (87.19% MPA, 80.36% MIoU). This is land-parcel/field-boundary mapping, not crop/weed pixel classification, so it is excluded under EXC-03.
DeepLab V3+ segments roads from UAV imagery in Malaysia for traffic/urban-planning applications (PA, mIoU, MeanF1). This is an urban/traffic domain, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.

This is a peer-review recommendation record ('Recommendation: ... R2/PR12') for a tree-crown semantic segmentation paper in forestry (mIoU 55.97%). It is secondary review literature in the forestry domain, excluded under EXC-05 and EXC-03.

This is an editorial decision record ('Decision: ... R3/PR17') for a tree-crown semantic segmentation paper in forestry. It is secondary editorial/review literature in the forestry domain, excluded under EXC-05 and EXC-03.

This is a peer-review recommendation record ('Recommendation: ... R0/PR3') for a tree-crown semantic segmentation paper in forestry. It is secondary review literature in the forestry domain, excluded under EXC-05 and EXC-03.

A UNet+ResNet18 global-local attention model achieves real-time segmentation (68%/67% mIoU, 72.4 FPS) on the UAvid and UDD6 datasets, which are urban/aerial general-scene datasets. It is not crop/weed agronomy, excluded under EXC-03.

This is an author-comment peer-review record ('Author comment: ... R1/PR5') for a tree-crown semantic segmentation paper in forestry. It is secondary review literature in the forestry domain, excluded under EXC-05 and EXC-03.

This is an author-comment peer-review record ('Author comment: ... R3/PR14') for a tree-crown semantic segmentation paper in forestry. It is secondary review literature in the forestry domain, excluded under EXC-05 and EXC-03.

Three DNNs perform real-time semantic segmentation of flood-affected regions on GPU edge platforms aboard UAVs (disaster scenario in Spain). This is a flood/disaster domain, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.
Combined segmentation networks (CSN) are trained on heterogeneous UAV datasets for urban-area class segmentation. This is an urban remote-sensing domain, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.
A ResNet50-UNet with Focal/Dice loss segments the Aeroscapes UAV dataset (F1 77.11, mIoU 65.26), which covers general aerial scene classes. It is not crop/weed agronomy, excluded under EXC-03.
DRSNet performs real-time foreground (people-scene) segmentation in rainy conditions on UESTC/Baidu person benchmarks. This is a general-object/people domain, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.
BiSeNet performs real-time aerial streetscape video segmentation on the USSD dataset (79.26% mIoU, 148.7 FPS). This is an urban streetscape domain, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.
UAV semantic segmentation maps urban greening/trees and classifies tree species (89.81% accuracy). This is an urban-vegetation/forestry domain, not agricultural crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.

No abstract is available despite a title indicating a real-time U-Net object segmentation system on aerial drone images; no retrievable quantitative results or crop/weed context exist. It is excluded under EXC-06.

A two-stage UAV localization method uses multi-category semantic segmentation + template matching to align with Baidu maps. This is a remote-sensing/localization domain, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.

FCN (32s/16s/8s) semantic segmentation is applied to the AeroScapes UAV remote-sensing dataset covering general aerial classes (vegetation ~94%, road ~88%). It is not crop/weed agronomy, excluded under EXC-03.
CNN semantic segmentation is evaluated on a general aerial-image dataset for architectural scene understanding, with no agricultural crop/weed content. It is excluded under EXC-03.

DeepLabV3+/FPN/LinkNet/etc. segment railway infrastructure (tracks, level crossings, vegetation) from UAV imagery on Jetson AGX Orin. This is infrastructure engineering, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.
eFPT is a Transformer-based 3D semantic segmentation network for post-disaster damage assessment on UAV-derived point clouds. This is a disaster-response domain, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.
A lightweight DeepLabV3+ (LSMA) segments sea/ship scenes from UAV imagery (MIoU 50.73%). This is a maritime domain, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.
A semantic-segmentation model validated on CityScapes and a campus dataset of Anhui University represents an urban/campus environment. It is not crop/weed agronomy, excluded under EXC-03.

UNet segments rice-field bunds (field levees/infrastructure) from UAV RGB imagery (99% accuracy). This is field-boundary infrastructure mapping rather than crop/weed pixel classification, so it is outside the target agronomic task under EXC-03.
YOLOv8 + DeepLabV3+ is used for intersection crowd monitoring and autonomous following (mAP 63.8%). This is an urban crowd-tracking domain, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.
A Hybrid U-Net segments high-resolution satellite imagery to identify conflict building devastation. The primary modality is satellite (EXC-01) and the domain is urban/civil, not crop/weed (EXC-03).
RS-BiseNet real-time aerial segmentation is evaluated on the ISPRS Potsdam urban land-cover dataset (2.96% MIoU gain). This is a general urban land-cover domain, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.
ATTransUNet segments buildings from aerial image + LiDAR for the MapAI competition (IoU 0.8555). This is an urban-buildings domain, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.

UAV aerial image stitching uses superpixel segmentation and SIFT feature matching to produce mosaics (SSIM/PSNR gains). This is image stitching/mosaicking, not crop/weed semantic segmentation, excluded under EXC-03 and EXC-02.

This Indonesian-language study uses YOLOv8 bounding-box object detection of tree objects for forest vegetation-density monitoring from UAV imagery (F1 up to 0.973). It is non-English (EXC-06), a forestry/bounding-box-detection task (EXC-03, EXC-02), and not crop/weed segmentation.
InfraRedSeg (Qwen2.5-VL + SAM2 point prompting) segments small infrared objects from UAV imagery for disaster response. This is a disaster-response domain, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.
DeepLabV3+ and other architectures segment cranes in post-earthquake UAV imagery (DeepLabV3+ mIoU 81.0%). This is a disaster-recovery domain, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.
SEC-BRNet (84.8% mIoU on AeroScapes, 62.81% on Semantic Drone Dataset) segments general UAV aerial classes. It is not crop/weed agronomy, excluded under EXC-03.

A GB-RBM-enhanced encoder-decoder segments ground vehicles from UAV thermal infrared imagery of Chinese city streets (average precision 0.97). This is an urban-vehicle domain, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.

CustomENet segments floating plastic waste in the aquatic environment of Dal Lake from UAV imagery (mIoU 0.7348, 43.61 FPS). This is an aquatic-plastic-pollution domain, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.

Marker-controlled watershed segmentation delineates individual tree crowns in a deciduous forest from UAS digital aerial photogrammetry. This is a non-deep-learning (EXC-04) forestry/tree domain (EXC-03), not crop/weed segmentation.
EDRSNet (51.61 FPS) real-time road extraction on DeepGlobe/DRS Road datasets supports UAV autonomous-vehicle navigation. This is a road-scene/navigation domain, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.

Unsupervised K-means and Gaussian Mixture Models (with NDVI interpretation) segment UAV multispectral winter-wheat orthomosaics. These are non-deep-learning unsupervised clustering methods with no learned crop/weed segmentation features, violating EXC-04.

A deep-learning semantic segmentation network delineates wetland ecosystems from UAV multispectral+TIR imagery (MPA 90.35%, MIOU 73.87%). This is an ecological-conservation/wetland domain, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.

This withdrawn preprint describes a deep-learning drone system for real-time detection/classification of structural damage (rust on metal roofs) in buildings. It is a civil-infrastructure domain, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.
Tree-crown semantic segmentation from aerial image time series identifies forest tree species (mIoU 55.97%). This is a forestry/tree-species domain, not agricultural crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.

A real-time branch-segmentation/grasp-localization framework (89.96% mIoU, 13.9 ms on Jetson Orin Nano) targets UAV interaction with natural tree branches. This is a forestry/natural-environment domain, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.

CRF/U-Net/FCN/DeepLabV3+ are analyzed on the ManipalUAVid campus aerial-video dataset (constructions, roads, waterbodies; mIoU up to 0.86). This is a general urban/campus scene domain, not crop/weed, excluded under EXC-03.

YOLO is used for bounding-box detection and Kalman-filter tracking/following of airborne UAVs (20 FPS on Neural Compute Stick 2). This is UAV-object detection/tracking, not agricultural crop/weed segmentation, excluded under EXC-03 and EXC-02.
